target_customer: Restaurants, hotels and cafeterias in Mexico buying food and supplies
problem: Small food service businesses order supplies from many vendors by phone; one place to order from a phone or WhatsApp saves time.
business_model: B2B marketplace take rate on wholesale supply orders

founders.name: Raul Maldonado
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former founder, a serial entrepreneur with cross border China trading experience.

founders.name: Marcelo Galvan
founders.background_notes: YC page bio describes a WhatsApp Commerce platform for SMB sales.

investors: Google for Startups Accelerator Latin Founders

competitors.name: Frubana
competitors.what: B2B wholesale marketplace and logistics for restaurants in Colombia, Mexico and Brazil

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering marketplace and WhatsApp commerce are standard engineering; operations and logistics are the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier and restaurant liquidity helps but better funded rivals could replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Frubana later closed Mexico and Colombia to focus on Brazil per Startups.com.br; no source shows it buying Boitas.

market_need_then: Fragmented Mexican food service supply with ordering done by phone and WhatsApp, enough for Frubana to raise $65M in 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Boitas had 35 people listed at YC and reported funding of only $130K to $539K depending on the database, small against Frubana's $65M. The YC directory lists it Inactive and the site returned 503, but no shutdown report or cause was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: Funding totals conflict: CB Insights $130K, Briter $539K; the Google accelerator round (Feb 2022) rests on CB Insights alone, amount not given. A seed entry dated March 2022 on another aggregator could not be tied to Boitas. Competitor source dated at batch or within months after (June 2021). Site boitas.com returned 503. Name origin not found.
